name: nextcloud-sync
description: Automatically sync a local Unraid folder with your Nextcloud using the official nextcloudcmd client. Features: - Continuous sync mode with configurable interval - Optional one-time run mode - Retry logic for temporary network/server issues - Non-root runtime (UID/GID 1001) - Minimal, security-focused Debian Trixie base image Recommended: use a Nextcloud app password/token instead of your main account password.

paths.name: Local Data Directory
paths.description: Local directory path synchronized with your Nextcloud account. Must be writable by the container.

variables.name: Nextcloud Username
variables.description: Your Nextcloud username. This is the username you use to log into your Nextcloud instance.

variables.name: Nextcloud Password/Token
variables.description: Your Nextcloud app password or token. For security reasons, it's highly recommended to create an app-specific password in Nextcloud Settings → Security → Devices & sessions instead of using your main password.

variables.name: Nextcloud Server URL
variables.description: Your Nextcloud server hostname or URL. Examples: cloud.example.com or https://cloud.example.com

variables.name: Sync Interval (seconds)
variables.description: Time interval between synchronization attempts in seconds. Default is 300 seconds (5 minutes). Increase for less frequent syncs or decrease for more frequent syncs.

variables.name: Sync Retry Attempts
variables.description: Number of retry attempts when synchronization fails (1-10 range). The container uses exponential backoff between retry attempts. Increase this value for unstable network connections. v2.7 includes enhanced retry logic with improved error handling and modern client compatibility.

variables.name: Run Once Mode
variables.description: Set to 'true' to run synchronization once and exit, or 'false' for continuous operation. Use 'true' for scheduled one-time syncs via Unraid User Scripts.

variables.name: Debug Logging
variables.description: Set to 'true' to enable verbose nextcloudcmd debug output (useful for troubleshooting).
